note: Authored, not generated. A fixture generated from one implementation records that implementation's beliefs, so a setting both sides get wrong stays invisible in two green suites at once. Each case states a governing policy and the client behaviour it must produce; both repositories carry this file byte-identically and replay their own copy against their own client factory. The redirect hop limit is deliberately absent: it is not a property of the transport stack on either side, it is an argument to the send loop, and asserting it here would compare nothing.

cases.name: defaults
cases.why: The shipped numbers. If the two implementations disagree about what an unstated policy means, every other case is comparing different baselines.

cases.name: narrowed
cases.why: An operator tightening both dials. The values are distinct from each other and from every default, so a factory that read one field into the other fails here rather than passing by coincidence.

cases.name: single-connection
cases.why: A ceiling of one is the boundary an off-by-one in the pool configuration would cross, and it is a real deployment shape for an upstream that serialises requests.

cases.name: wide
cases.why: A high ceiling with a long dial. Decompression and the disabled redirect follow must not become conditional on the numbers, and the per-client deadline must stay absent no matter how generous the policy is.
